Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

MemberChangeReason.description: The reason carried by one member's change in a messaging/mux/event `attached` or `detached` event: exactly the AttachReason values followed by the DetachReason values, with their meanings. An `attached` event carries only AttachReason values and a `detached` event only DetachReason values. One closed set rather than a union, so every generated binding types it as one enumeration; it MUST be kept equal to the two sets it joins.
MemberChangeReason.title: MemberChangeReason

MembershipChange.description: What happened to a member DID's place on a mux connection, as messaging/mux/event reports it to the connection's principal. `attached`: the member joined the connection, or its scope or expiry there changed. `detached`: the member left the connection, or a stored grant of it was not attached on connect.
MembershipChange.title: MembershipChange

MonitorEvent.description: One observed step in the life of one message at the mediator. Carries metadata only — never a message body.

from.description: The sender, where the mediator knows it.

latencyMs.description: For `delivered` and `forwarded`: milliseconds since the message was stored.

messageType.description: The plaintext message type, present only when the mediator itself was the addressee and read it (a routing forward, a pickup request, a trust-task type URI, a trust ping). Absent for end-to-end-encrypted traffic the mediator only relays.

msgId.description: The stored message's identifier, once it has one; correlates the events of one message and matches MessageMeta.msgId.

occurredAt.description: When the step happened, with sub-second precision where the mediator has it.

outcome.description: Present when stage is `refused`, and on any other stage that failed.

to.description: The recipient, where the mediator knows it.

MonitorEvent.title: MonitorEvent

MonitorMembershipEvent.description: One change to the membership of one mux connection at the mediator: a member DID attached to or detached from a principal's connection. Not a step in the life of a message, so it is not a MonitorEvent and carries none of its members. Carries metadata only — never a message, a signed statement, a nonce or key material.

member.description: The member DID that attached or detached, in the same form the mediator uses for accounts.

occurredAt.description: When the change took effect, with sub-second precision where the mediator has it.

principal.description: The DID the connection is authenticated as, in the same form the mediator uses for accounts.

reason.description: Why, exactly as the messaging/mux/event entry for the change reports it: an AttachReason value when `change` is `attached`, a DetachReason value when it is `detached`.

sessionId.description: The connection's identifier, as its `ready` event announced it and messaging/mux/connections lists it. Absent when the mediator does not report it.

source.description: Whether the member rides, or rode, the connection through a stored grant or a session attach.

MonitorMembershipEvent.title: MonitorMembershipEvent

MuxSource.description: How a member came to be on a connection: through a stored grant, or through a session attach bound to that connection.
MuxSource.title: MuxSource

MuxWire.description: The wire a mux connection speaks: `didcomm`, a DIDComm WebSocket that negotiated the `didcomm-mux` subprotocol; `tsp`, a raw-TSP WebSocket that negotiated `tsp-mux`. The same values messaging/mux/connections reports for a connection's `wire`.
MuxWire.title: MuxWire

SessionId.description: The mediator's identifier for one authenticated connection, as announced in that connection's `ready` event.
SessionId.title: SessionId

TrafficChannel.description: How the traffic reached or left the mediator. `peerMediator` is mediator-to-mediator forwarding.
TrafficChannel.title: TrafficChannel

TrafficDirection.description: `inbound`: arriving at the mediator. `outbound`: leaving it (delivery to a recipient, or a forward to another mediator). `internal`: a state change with no wire traffic (expiry, deletion, purge).
TrafficDirection.title: TrafficDirection

TrafficOutcome.description: Why a frame was refused or failed.

code.description: The stable error code the mediator returned to the sender (a trust-task-error or problem-report code).

TrafficOutcome.title: TrafficOutcome

TrafficStage.description: What happened. `received`: a frame arrived. `stored`: it was queued for a local account. `delivered`: handed to its recipient. `forwarded`: relayed to another mediator. `refused`: rejected (see the event's `outcome`). `deleted`: removed by its recipient or an administrator. `expired`: removed by expiry. `purged`: removed by a queue purge.
TrafficStage.title: TrafficStage

Vid.description: A Verifiable Identifier (SPEC §4.8). For a mediator-served account this is the account's controlling DID, carried verbatim and compared by exact string equality. For privacy — and because some mediators key accounts by a one-way hash and never hold the full DID — a stable hash of the DID (e.g. its SHA-256 digest) is an equally valid value here: producer and consumer simply agree on the same opaque identifier and compare by exact string equality. The field carries whichever form the issuing mediator uses.
Vid.title: Vid

WireProtocol.description: The protocol a message travelled in, as the mediator detected it from the wire form. `didcomm` is DIDComm v2 (JWE/JWS); `didcommV1` is a DIDComm v1 envelope; `tsp` is a Trust Spanning Protocol message; `other` is anything the mediator could not classify.
WireProtocol.title: WireProtocol

dropped.description: Traffic events that matched the filter but were discarded since the previous batch — rate ceiling exceeded or subscriber not connected. Membership events are counted in `membershipDropped`, never here.

events.description: Traffic events in the order the mediator observed them. May be empty on a heartbeat batch, and is always empty on a subscription that turned traffic events off.

expiresAt.description: The subscription's current expiry, so the subscriber can renew before it lapses.

membership.description: Mux membership events, in the order the mediator observed them. Present only on a subscription that opted in to them with messaging/monitor/subscribe `membership`, and then on every batch, empty when there is nothing to report.

membershipDropped.description: Membership events that matched the subscription's membership filter but were discarded since the previous batch. Present exactly when `membership` is.

seq.description: Batch sequence number, starting at 1 and increasing by exactly 1 per batch within a subscription. A gap means batches were lost in transit.
